_comment: Tool-call GATE policy for the harness (harness/audit.py). This file decides which tool calls are HIGH-RISK and what happens to them BEFORE the tool runs — independently of which front-end is driving (SDK orchestrator, DeepSeek/OpenAI shim, or the stdio MCP server used by Claude Code). Three risk classes are named here: OUTBOUND (the call touches target infrastructure from your IP, so a hostile operator can see you), METERED (the call spends third-party API credits that are per-account and do not roll over), and APPROVAL-REQUIRED (the call is outbound AND attributable AND irreversible — a sandbox submission tells the operator they are being analysed). Every call, allowed or denied, is written to the ledger at cases/<case>/tool_calls.jsonl. Edit the lists below to re-classify a tool; you do not need to touch Python. Tool names are matched on the BARE name, so both `pivot_extract` and the SDK's fully-qualified `mcp__collect__pivot_extract` match the same entry.

outbound_tools._comment: Tools whose normal mode reaches the TARGET's infrastructure from the analyst's own IP (live HTTP fetch, DNS to attacker-controlled nameservers, screenshot, sandbox submission). Under hostile posture (--hostile, or HARNESS_HOSTILE=1) a call to one of these is DENIED unless it also carries one of `passive_args` below. This is the same rule pivot_extract already enforces internally; listing a tool here lifts the rule ABOVE the tool, so it covers every collector, not just the one that remembered to implement it. `doc_metadata` is listed because it CAN fetch a URL — under hostile posture, read a file you have already pulled out-of-band by running WebPivot/tools/wp_docmeta.py on the local path instead. `serp_ads` is listed for its cloak mode only: the archive lookups are pure SerpApi traffic, but the cloaking probe fetches the TARGET three times from your own IP and, by design, announces itself as an ad click — under hostile posture route it through --proxy or skip it.

passive_args._comment: Arguments that make an outbound call safe under hostile posture: the traffic either never leaves your machine or does not originate from your IP. If any of these is truthy in the call's arguments, the hostile denial does not apply. `passive` means archive/third-party sources only; `proxy` routes the fetch elsewhere; `free_only` implies the keyless/passive path.

metered_tools._comment: Tools that CAN spend licensed third-party API credits (FOFA, urlscan, WhoisXML, IPinfo, Shodan, Censys, IntelX, ANY.RUN, SerpApi). These are never blocked outright — collection is the job — but they are counted against `budget.max_metered_calls_per_run` and every call lands in the ledger, so 'what did this run spend' is answerable after the fact rather than guessed. Censys is the tightest quota (100 credits per MONTH, per account, no rollover), which is why an over-budget run is stopped rather than warned.

free_only_args._comment: Arguments that PROVE a call spends nothing, so it must not be counted against the metered budget. A run driven by the convergence loop passes free_only=true on every collection, which is why such a run can be long without touching a single credit. Note what is NOT here: `passive` and `proxy` protect your IP from the target, they do not protect your credits — a passive run still queries urlscan and WhoisXML. Keep the two concerns separate or a hostile-posture run will silently drain the month's Censys quota.

metered_arg_triggers._comment: Arguments that turn an otherwise-cheap call into an expensive one. A bare pivot_extract already costs a few credits; with these set it fans out into reverse-WHOIS or a full FOFA page and costs many more. Present here only so the ledger records WHY a call was scored expensive — they do not change the allow/deny decision on their own.

approval_required_tools._comment: Tools that are outbound AND attributable AND irreversible, and therefore need a human 'yes' that a prompt cannot supply. Each maps to the environment variable that must be set to 1 for the call to be permitted; without it the call is DENIED before it reaches the tool. anyrun_submit detonates a sample or URL in a sandbox: a URL detonation tells the operator they are being analysed, the task may be PUBLIC on a free plan, and nothing can be recalled once sent. engage_account CREATES AN ACCOUNT on the operator's own backend and logs in: the operator sees a new member at a known time from your egress, and you cannot un-register. misp_publish SHARES the case's indicators: MISP pushes the event to every server the instance synchronises with and notifies subscribers, so a wrong indicator becomes other people's blocking rule and deleting your copy deletes nothing of theirs — note that its sibling misp_push is NOT listed here on purpose, because a push is clamped in code to an organisation-only, unpublished event that has reached nobody and can be deleted. None of these is 'outbound' in the hostile-egress sense (they do not touch the target from your IP), so they are not in outbound_tools; the risk is irreversibility, not exposure. Each of these tools also has its OWN internal confirmation gate (a confirm flag in the signature) — this entry is the second lock, so an agent loop cannot reach the first one unattended.

approval_briefing._comment: The read-only BRIEFING branch of an approval-required tool, which must stay reachable WITHOUT the approval env var — otherwise the two-step 'show the analyst the risk briefing, ask, then confirm' gate is impossible in the MCP/harness path, because the briefing call itself would be denied. Maps a tool to the argument names that must ALL be falsy for the exemption to apply: when every one is absent/false the call does nothing outbound or irreversible (it composes the briefing offline), so it is allowed; set any of them and the call is the real, gated action again. anyrun_submit: `confirm` (the POST that detonates) and `verify_task` (reads a task and can DELETE it) — with neither, submit() only returns submit_preflight(). Leave a tool out to keep it fully gated. This exemption never applies under hostile posture (an outbound tool is still egress-blocked there).

mutating_tools._comment: Tools that write to shared, cross-case state (the knowledge base, the benign/signal reference, the operator registry, a MISP instance). Never blocked, but flagged in the ledger: when a later case turns out to have clustered on a bad fingerprint — or when someone asks which indicators we put on the sharing platform and when — this is how you find the run and the round that did it.

redact_args._comment: Argument-name FRAGMENTS whose VALUE is never written to the ledger verbatim (replaced with '<redacted>'). Matched as SUBSTRINGS of the normalised name (lowercased, '_' and '-' removed), at any nesting depth — so 'key' covers apiKey, x_api_key and X-Api-Key, 'token' covers access_token, 'pass' covers password and passwd, 'auth' covers Authorization. Only the declared boolean parameters in redact_bool_switches keep a switch value (passive=true, secrets=true); any other secret-named argument is redacted whatever its value, so password='true' or token='1' never reaches disk. Independently of the name, every string value is scrubbed of URL userinfo (http://user:pass@host -> http://<redacted>@host), of query parameters whose name matches a fragment (?token=…&apikey=…), and of 'Bearer <token>' strings; the host, path and non-secret parameters stay readable. Ledger files live under cases/, which is git-ignored, but a credential pasted into a tool argument should still never be persisted to disk in cleartext. Add a fragment for any argument that could carry a key, token or password — and check it is not a substring of an ordinary argument name.

redact_bool_switches._comment: Declared BOOLEAN tool parameters whose names contain a redact_args fragment (passive ⊃ 'pass', secrets ⊃ 'secret'). Only these names keep a boolean value (true/false/yes/no/1/0) in the ledger, because the audit trail needs to show whether a call ran passive; any other secret-named argument is redacted even when its value looks boolean. Add a name here only when tool_params.json declares it type boolean.

budget._comment: Per-run guard rails. max_metered_calls_per_run caps how many credit-spending calls ONE run may make before the gate starts denying them with an instruction to re-call free_only=true — the backstop against an agent loop that keeps re-querying FOFA on every round. Set generously: it exists to stop runaway loops, not to ration normal collection. Override at runtime with HARNESS_METERED_BUDGET. max_arg_chars truncates long argument values in the ledger so one HTML blob cannot bloat the audit trail.

proposal_gated_tools._comment: Cross-type loop approval gate (harness/proposal.py). While a case's loop is active (cases/<case>/proposal.json loop_active=true), a METERED call to one of these tools is DENIED unless it matches an item the analyst approved in that round's digest-current proposal — the per-round consent rule is enforced here, at the gate every front-end shares, not by the prompt. Outside an active loop the tools behave as before. These are the pivot tools the loop proposes; the collect phase's own collectors are not listed.

route_metered_tools._comment: Tools whose meteredness depends on a ROUTE argument: tool -> argument name. The route is looked up in harness/references/pivot_map.json routes.<route>.metered (urlscan routes are quota-backed and not metered; fofa/publicwww/rwhois purchase/anyrun are). An unknown route counts as metered.

arg_metered_tools._comment: Tools that spend ONLY when an argument is truthy: tool -> argument name. search_pivot builds dork URLs offline by default; with run=true it executes them, DuckDuckGo first (free) and SerpApi Google (1 metered search per query) for any query the free path could not answer. Counted as metered only then, and free_only=true keeps it on the free path (it is in free_only_capable_tools).

operator_only_tools._comment: The analyst's consent step for the cross-type loop. Denied whenever the call comes from a harness PHASE (collect/correlate/verify/assess/plan…), allowed only interactively — otherwise the loop could approve its own metered pivots.

free_only_capable_tools._comment: Metered tools whose handler HONOURS free_only (has a keyless mode): pivot_extract → the collector's --free-only, reverse_whois → free preview count only, deep_profile / case_enrich → their own free-only legs, corpus_search → keyless urlscan + metered routes skipped. The gate classes a free_only call as not-metered and lets it through, so every OTHER metered tool refuses free_only=true instead of spending (harness/tools.py _free_only_refusal). Add a tool here only after its handler really honours the flag.
